claim: Among locals (not tourists), Pequod's edges out Lou Malnati's for deep dish, prized for its caramelized cheese ring from cast-iron pans; Lou Malnati's wins on accessibility, affordability, and sauce.
quote: When asking locals—not tourists—where to get deep dish, Pequod's comes up more than any other name... each pie develops a ring of caramelized mozzarella around the edges that's crispy, almost burnt, and utterly addictive.

claim: Chicago natives prefer thin tavern-style pizza, calling it the 'one true' Chicago style, while deep dish is largely a tourist phenomenon; older tavern institutions include Vito & Nick's, Granato's, and Aurelio's.
quote: the first to correct you on the differences between deep dish and tavern-style pizza, pointing out that the latter is the 'one true' Chicago style of pizza.

claim: Tavern-style is defined by an ultra-thin crispy crust cut into small squares for sharing, while deep dish is a thick, sauce-and-cheese-layered pie baked in a round pan requiring a sit-down meal.
quote: tavern-style pizza is defined primarily by its base of ultra-thin and crispy crust, and a tavern-style pizza is typically circular but is then cut into small squares, perfect for sharing at a tavern.

claim: The Infatuation ranks Al's #1 Italian Beef (Taylor St, Little Italy) as Chicago's top Italian beef; Al's is credited with inventing the sandwich in 1938; Mr. Beef (River North, the inspiration for The Bear) ranks #7 but is iconic.
quote: Al's #1 Italian Beef... claims the top spot... credited with inventing the Italian beef sandwich in 1938... Mr. Beef in River North ranks #7... described as 'iconic' and inspired by The Bear television series.

claim: Vito & Nick's (South Side, since the 1950s) is widely held as Chicago's premier tavern-style pizza, with a crust that stays crispy edge-to-center under bubbly browned cheese.
quote: From edge to center, Vito and Nick's thin crust stays equally crispy, despite the thick layer of bubbly brown cheese and pepperoni... a Southside institution worthy of its place in the Chicago Pizza Hall of Fame.

claim: Four Chicago bars made North America's 50 Best Bars list, led by Kumiko at #11 (also named Best Bar in the Midwest), Julia Momose's Japanese-influenced cocktail program.
quote: Four Chicago cocktail bars made North America's 50 Best Bars list in 2026, with Kumiko leading at number 11 and also earning the Best Bar in the Midwest title... Julia Momose, offers splurge-worthy concoctions... rice vodka, saké vermouth and umé.

claim: Standout Chicago cocktail bars include The Aviary (West Loop, theatrical), Three Dots and a Dash (River North tiki), Billy Sunday (Logan Square, amaro-focused), and Meadowlark (Logan Square, themed cocktails).
quote: The Aviary offers a theatrical cocktail experience in West Loop... Three Dots and a Dash serves tiki cocktails... Billy Sunday focuses on amaro-focused drinks... Meadowlark in Logan Square is cozy and intimate, with each cocktail tied to a theme.

claim: WBEZ readers named Revolution Brewing, Half Acre, Moody Tongue, Dovetail, Off Color, Begyle, Old Irving, and Hop Butcher for the World among Chicago's favorite craft breweries; Marz Community Brewing also a frequent mention.
quote: Industry Ales, Hop Butcher for the World, Begyle Brewing, Suncatcher Brewing, Old Irving Brewing Co., Revolution Brewing, Dovetail Brewery, Off Color Brewing, Half Acre Beer Co., Moody Tongue.

claim: Top Chicago breakfast/brunch picks span the classic diner Lou Mitchell's, seasonal Logan Square pioneer Lula Cafe (opened 1999), S.K.Y. in Lincoln Park, and Swedish institution Ann Sather in Andersonville.
quote: Lou Mitchell's and Obelix are among the institutions... Lula Cafe, which opened in 1999, helped turn Logan Square into a dining destination... Ann Sather in Andersonville highlights the neighborhood's Swedish history with airy Swedish pancakes.

claim: Half Acre's north-side taproom built a following on its Daisy Cutter Pale Ale, Goose Island's Fulton Market brewery is known for barrel-aging, and Revolution Brewing's Anti-Hero IPA is a city staple with a full destination taproom.
quote: Half Acre's north-side taproom... Their Daisy Cutter Pale Ale alone built a devoted following... Revolution is arguably the most recognizable name in Chicago craft beer, with their Anti-Hero IPA becoming a city staple.
